title: Ang 1385–1389: Guru Arjan's swayyas
tomorrow: court poets praise the Gurus themselves. what do they hear in them?

cards: A couple says I love you every single day, and a friend teases: doesn't she know by now?
On ang 1385, Guru Arjan writes pages of praise to the One: the first Being, the Creator, the cause of all causes, everything Himself. These are swayyas, verses with a rolling, ringing beat.
And they raise yesterday's question, one Sikhs really do ask: does the One need any of it?

teach.b: Here are two answers, each in its best form. The first: no. Praise is for the one who sings.
The One isn't made bigger by anyone's words. But a person who praises, morning after morning, turns toward something larger than their own worries, and that turning changes them.
On this view, the swayyas are training: attention pointed up. The second: praise isn't a tool at all.

teach.h: TWO: PRAISE IS LOVE SAID ALOUD.
teach.b: It's love said out loud. Nobody says I love you because it's useful. They say it because it's true and it wants out.
On this view, the swayyas are what a heart sounds like when it overflows, and asking whether God needs it is like asking whether a grandmother needs a hug. Both readings live inside Sikh devotion.
The Granth is full of praise, and full of reminders that the One is beyond it. Guru Arjan's swayyas don't settle it.
They just keep going: Creator, cause of causes, everywhere, beyond counting. Nobody has to choose today. Listen to what each side guards.
One guards honesty: the One needs nothing.
The other guards warmth: love speaks.

how: Guru Arjan's swayyas are read in the Granth's closing pages and sung in kirtan; Sikh teachers speak of praise, sifat salah, both as turning the mind and as love's own voice.

o: where the ninth Guru's last saloks begin
where Farid calls every heart a jewel
where Guru Arjan's verses of praise begin

games.q: Guru Arjan's swayyas — tap the pairs.
p: verses of praise, a ringing beat
praise is love said out loud

s: in Sikh thought, God grows greater when praised
one reading is the reverse: the One needs nothing, and praise changes the singer.
Guru Arjan's swayyas call the Creator the cause of all causes
they open on the first Being, the Creator, the cause of all causes.
the swayyas argue for one answer about why people praise
they don't argue. they keep praising, and leave the question open.

games.q: your friend says praying with praise is like flattering a boss. before you answer, what's the best case for 'praise is for the singer'?
o: the One needs nothing, so praise is attention turned upward, and the turning changes the one who sings.
God enjoys flattery, so the more praise you give, the more blessings come back to you.
praise does nothing at all, so the swayyas were written only to be beautiful poems.
games.why: that's the first answer at its best. the second answer at its best: praise isn't a tool, it's love said out loud. Guru Arjan's swayyas hold room for both.

practice: Say one line of praise out loud for something good you can see from where you are: the light, a person, a cup of tea. Then sit in the quiet after it, and notice which of today's two answers your line leaned toward.
